description: App web ágil que combina datos satelitales (NASA, CONAE, AEB) por lote para alertar anomalías y sugerir rotación de cultivos, enfocada (por ahora) en Argentina ante problemáticas locales. ¡Cualquier perfil es bienvenido, sin importar país o profesión! Buscamos sobre todo devs fullstack/GIS, agrónomos y expertos en teledetección para llevar la solución al campo. ¡Sumate! Ojo que para unirse deben NO estar en otro equipo
summary:
ARGFIELD is a web-based agricultural decision-support platform designed for Argentine farms. It integrates NASA Earth observation data, satellite imagery, weather forecasts, regional agricultural statistics, and farmer-provided information into a unified interface.

Farmers can register their location, crops, soil characteristics, irrigation conditions, and cultivation history to explore environmental conditions and evaluate alternative crop rotations.

At its core, ARGFIELD uses NASA POWER historical climate data and a multi-criteria optimization engine to compare crop rotation strategies based on water availability, thermal suitability, soil compatibility, diversification, and regional stability.

The platform also provides interactive satellite maps, weather alerts, hypothetical climate stress scenarios, and traceable reports.

ARGFIELD aims to make complex environmental data more accessible and actionable, supporting informed agricultural planning without replacing field measurements or professional agronomic advice.
details:
How does ARGFIELD work?

ARGFIELD transforms publicly available environmental information into an integrated agricultural decision-support experience.

Users begin by creating a farm profile containing its geographic location, cultivated area, current and previous crops, soil type, irrigation conditions, and production priorities.

Based on the selected location, the platform retrieves climate information, satellite observations, and historical agricultural data. These inputs are organized into an interactive dashboard with weather conditions, environmental indicators, geographical layers, and relevant alerts.

Satellite and Environmental Data

ARGFIELD integrates multiple Earth observation products, including NASA POWER, SMAP, GPM IMERG, MODIS, Sentinel imagery, and Argentina's CONAE satellite resources.

These datasets provide complementary information about historical climate, precipitation, soil moisture, vegetation conditions, and land surface temperature.

Every available observation includes information about its source, observation date, and data status. Missing or outdated observations are explicitly identified rather than replaced with artificial values.

Crop Rotation Optimization

The platform includes a multi-criteria crop rotation evaluation engine.

It combines NASA POWER historical climate records, regional agricultural statistics, farm characteristics, agronomic parameters, and crop succession rules to compare feasible rotation alternatives.

The engine evaluates factors such as:

  • Thermal suitability and water compatibility.
  • Soil characteristics and crop succession.
  • Crop diversification and soil coverage.
  • Historical regional production stability.
  • User-defined agricultural priorities.

Incompatible crop sequences are excluded before scoring.

Users can also explore hypothetical scenarios involving reduced rainfall, increased temperatures, or combined climatic stress to understand how different rotation alternatives respond to changing conditions.

These scenarios are sensitivity analyses, not climate forecasts.

Technology and Implementation

ARGFIELD was developed as a web application using TypeScript, React, Vite, and modern web technologies.

Leaflet provides interactive geographic visualization, while external environmental data services supply satellite, climate, and agricultural information.

The platform integrates NASA POWER, Open-Meteo, CONAE, Copernicus-related resources, and regional agricultural datasets.

An AI-assisted summary feature helps explain the available information in accessible language. The AI does not generate environmental measurements or determine crop rotation rankings.

Innovation and Impact

ARGFIELD's main innovation is combining heterogeneous environmental datasets with transparent, rule-based agricultural evaluation in a single accessible platform.

Rather than presenting isolated satellite observations, it connects environmental context with farm-specific information and agricultural planning alternatives.

The system emphasizes transparency, data provenance, and uncertainty. Users can distinguish observed measurements, historical statistics, model-derived scores, and hypothetical scenarios.

ARGFIELD is intended to support agricultural professionals and producers in exploring crop rotation strategies, understanding environmental constraints, and making better-informed decisions.

It does not replace field measurements, locally calibrated agronomic models, or professional recommendations.
